market_context: United States/general English; firm tofu and cooked skinless chicken breast
title: Tofu vs. chicken: nutrition comparison

seo.title: Tofu vs. chicken: protein, calories, fat, and nutrients
seo.meta_description: Chicken breast is more protein-dense at about 31 g/100 g versus roughly 12–17 g in firm tofu. Tofu adds unsaturated fat, iron, and sometimes calcium.
seo.search_intent: Compare tofu and chicken as protein sources for amount, calories, fat, protein quality, and micronutrients.

excerpt: Cooked chicken breast is substantially more protein-dense than tofu: about 31 g protein per 100 g versus roughly 12–17 g in firm tofu. Both can provide complete protein, but the nutrient packages differ: chicken is leaner and rich in B12, niacin, and selenium; tofu provides mostly unsaturated fat, iron, and can be very high in calcium when made with calcium salts.
content_html:
Tofu and chicken can fill the same role on a plate—the main protein source—but they do not provide the same amount of protein at the same weight. Cooked chicken breast is much more concentrated. Tofu contains more water, and its protein content changes with firmness and manufacturing.

Chicken is more protein-dense

A representative comparison between cooked skinless chicken breast and firm tofu looks like this:

Per 100 gCooked chicken breastFirm tofu
Protein~31 g~12–17 g
Calories~165 kcal~120–145 kcal
Fat~3.6 g~7–9 g
Carbohydrate~0 g~2–3 g

The protein gap can be 14–19 g per 100 g. To approach the 31 g protein in 100 g chicken breast, you may need roughly 180–250 g tofu, depending on the product.

A meal-size serving narrows the practical gap

A 5-ounce chicken breast serving, about 142 g, provides roughly 44 g protein. Eight ounces of firm tofu, about 227 g, at 15 g protein per 100 g provides about 34 g.

Both amounts can anchor a high-protein meal. Saying tofu has less protein per 100 g is accurate; saying it cannot provide enough protein is not.

Both contain all essential amino acids

Soy provides all nine essential amino acids and is considered a high-quality plant protein. Chicken also provides complete protein and generally has somewhat higher digestibility.

In a varied diet, that does not make tofu an incomplete protein or require it to be paired with rice at the same meal.

The fat profiles tell a different story

Firm tofu often contains more total fat than very lean chicken breast, but most of that fat is unsaturated. Chicken breast is lower in fat in this specific cut; thighs with skin, wings, or fried chicken can be far higher.

“Chicken” therefore is not one fixed nutrition number. Skinless breast is one of the leanest cuts.

Iron and calcium can favor tofu

Firm tofu often provides around 2–3 mg non-heme iron per 100 g. Chicken breast generally provides less, often around 1 mg or below.

Tofu calcium varies enormously. Calcium-set tofu can contain several hundred milligrams per 100 g, while tofu made with other coagulants may contain much less. The label is especially useful here.

Chicken naturally provides nutrients tofu does not

Chicken breast is rich in niacin, vitamin B6, selenium, and vitamin B12. Tofu is not a reliable natural source of B12 unless fortified.

Tofu, in return, brings soy compounds and small amounts of fiber that meat does not contain.

Which is better?

If you want maximum protein in a smaller amount of food with very little fat, chicken breast has a clear advantage. If you want a complete plant protein that can also contribute iron, calcium, and unsaturated fat, tofu works very well.

They do not need to match gram for gram. The right serving size and the rest of the diet matter more than making tofu nutritionally imitate chicken.

faq.question: Which has more protein, tofu or chicken?
faq.answer: Cooked chicken breast provides about 31 g protein per 100 g; firm tofu is commonly around 12–17 g.

faq.question: Is tofu a complete protein?
faq.answer: Yes. Soy protein contains all nine essential amino acids.

faq.question: Does tofu have more calcium than chicken?
faq.answer: It can have dramatically more if it is set with calcium salts, but tofu calcium varies widely, so check the label.
